questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A Copper wire of length $L_{\mathrm{Cu}}$, Young's modulus $Y_{\mathrm{Cu}}$, and diameter $d$ is hung from the ceiling. An Aluminium wire of length $L_{\mathrm{Al}}$, Young's modulus $Y_{\mathrm{Al}}$, and of same diameter $d$ is joined end-to-end at the free end of the Copper wire. If under the action of a load applied at the free end of the Aluminium wire the net elongation is $\Delta L$, the applied load is
options: $\frac{\pi d^2 \Delta L\left(Y_{\mathrm{Cu}} L_{\mathrm{Al}}-Y_{\mathrm{Al}} L_{\mathrm{Cu}}\right)}{4 L_{\mathrm{Cu}} L_{\mathrm{Al}}}$.
$\frac{\pi d^2 \Delta L\left(Y_{\mathrm{Cu}} L_{\mathrm{Al}}+Y_{\mathrm{Al}} L_{\mathrm{Cu}}\right)}{4 L_{\mathrm{Cu}} L_{\mathrm{Al}}}$.
$\frac{\pi d^2 Y_{\mathrm{Cu}} Y_{\mathrm{Al}} \Delta L}{4\left(Y_{\mathrm{Cu}} L_{\mathrm{Al}}+Y_{\mathrm{Al}} L_{\mathrm{Cu}}\right)}$.
$\frac{\pi d^2 Y_{\mathrm{Cu}} Y_{\mathrm{Al}} \Delta L}{4\left(Y_{\mathrm{Cu}} L_{\mathrm{Al}}-Y_{\mathrm{Al}} L_{\mathrm{Cu}}\right)}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An exotic spherical jellyfish has a bulk modulus $B$. Close to the surface of the sea (depth $d=0$), its radius is $R$. When it dives to a depth $d$ ($d \gg R$), its radius is reduced by $\Delta R \gt  0$. Given the density of the incompressible sea water $\rho$, and the uniform acceleration due to gravity $g$ such that $\rho g d \ll B$, what is $\dfrac{\Delta R}{R}$?
questions.solution:
The change in pressure at a depth $d$ is given by $\Delta P = \rho g d$.

The bulk modulus $B$ is defined as the ratio of volumetric stress to volumetric strain:

$B = -\dfrac{\Delta P}{\dfrac{\Delta V}{V}}$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{\Delta V}{V} = -\dfrac{\rho g d}{B}$

The new volume $V'$ of the jellyfish at depth $d$ is:

$V' = V + \Delta V = V\left(1 - \dfrac{\rho g d}{B}\right)$

Since the jellyfish is spherical, its volume is proportional to the cube of its radius ($V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3$). The new radius is $R - \Delta R$, so the ratio of the new volume to the initial volume is:

$\dfrac{V'}{V} = \left(\dfrac{R - \Delta R}{R}\right)^3 = \left(1 - \dfrac{\Delta R}{R}\right)^3$

Equating the two expressions for $\dfrac{V'}{V}$:

$\left(1 - \dfrac{\Delta R}{R}\right)^3 = 1 - \dfrac{\rho g d}{B}$

Taking the cube root on both sides:

$1 - \dfrac{\Delta R}{R} = \left(1 - \dfrac{\rho g d}{B}\right)^{1/3}$

$\dfrac{\Delta R}{R} = 1 - \left(1 - \dfrac{\rho g d}{B}\right)^{1/3}$

Answer: $\left[1 - \left(1 - \dfrac{\rho g d}{B}\right)^{1/3}\right]$
